title: Tool-Using Agent with Safety Controls
subtitle: Give an agent useful tools while controlling identity, approvals, effects, budgets and recovery outside the model.
theme: Agents and Copilots in Real Workflows
author: By Sourav Banerjee

practice_prompts.label: Authority, money boundary and stakeholders
practice_prompts.hint: Which actions are reversible, whose identity the agent uses, what needs approval, and what each stakeholder notices first.

practice_prompts.label: Trace the email-to-refund request
practice_prompts.hint: Follow one proposal through registry, validation, policy, approval, broker, gateway and receipt.

practice_prompts.label: Injection, lost response and stale approval
practice_prompts.hint: Say where each failure is caught, what fails closed and how an unknown outcome is reconciled.

practice_prompts.label: Release gates and the refund near miss
practice_prompts.hint: Name the two zero counts, the rollout order and how you separate planner failure from gateway success.

rubric: Separates proposer, policy authority and execution receipt.
Validates exact payload and current approval before writes.
Explains idempotency contract and unknown-outcome reconciliation.
Bounds steps, value, destinations and concurrent work.
Shows a real in-flight containment plan and its limits.
Releases by observed unsafe/duplicate effects and accountable owners.
Diagnoses a looping or slow agent by bounding steps before optimising, with safe cache keys.

editorial_review.evidence: Compared all 58 captured sections against the earlier draft paragraph by paragraph. The draft's coverage was templated: it dropped the five-row stakeholder map, the three answer tiers, the seven-step whiteboard architecture, sync/async boundaries, the injection replay that its own figure depicts, the model-to-tool time ratio, the risk register table, the who-decides integration axis and Salesforce mapping, cost scenarios' later/prevent steps and cache-key rule, the near-miss scorecard and spoken answer, and every memorable interview quote; it also gave three different plane figures one caption and said a 'refund ledger' owned refund history. These are restored in the walkthrough and deep dives; six follow-ups became answer-11 to answer-16. Our own qualifications (combined 43.2 GB/day audit total, model API sized by concurrency not cores, 'no unauthorised money' is not 'no money', kill-switch limits, distinct identities for identical refunds) are marked as ours. The brief now defines bounded action, deterministic service and idempotent gateway before use and maps the related variant cases. November 20 complete maintained-baseline review: Complete maintained five-section casebook: eight walkthrough steps, eleven protected figures, action records and receipts, four security controls, all workload arithmetic, 18-call refund near miss, integration protocols, practice answers and source notes.
